objects.description: Represents an absolute point in time in UTC with nanosecond precision, stored as seconds since Unix epoch plus an additional nanoseconds field. Provides construction from raw seconds/nanoseconds, current time, time_t, and std::chrono::time_point; conversion back to time_point; string formatting; and comparison operators. Bounds checking is performed to ensure the representable Gregorian calendar range [0001-01-01, 9999-12-31] and nanoseconds in [0, 999,999,999]. Destruction has no special requirements (trivially copyable/movable).

Immutable value type representing a geographical coordinate (latitude, longitude) for Firestore documents. Provides constructors, trivial copy/move semantics, accessors, string conversion, stream output, and comparison operators. Latitude must be within [-90, 90] and longitude within [-180, 180]. Enforcement details are not shown here; validation may occur in the out-of-line constructor implementation.

Enumeration of Firestore error codes in the firebase::firestore namespace. Provides symbolic constants for error reporting and handling; kErrorOk and kErrorNone both map to 0 (success). Use as a value type; no dynamic construction or ownership semantics apply.
A global constant pointer to a null-terminated C string containing the Firebase Firestore SDK version. Defined elsewhere; only declared in this header.

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::Timestamp
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates a Timestamp at Unix epoch (seconds = 0, nanoseconds = 0). Useful for initializing to a known zero value.

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::Timestamp
functions.description: Constructs a Timestamp from explicit seconds since Unix epoch and nanoseconds. Asserts if values are out of the supported range.
requirements: seconds must be within 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z inclusive (interpreted as seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z)
nanoseconds must be in the range [0, 999,999,999]
If seconds is negative and represents a time before epoch, nanoseconds must still be non-negative and count forward in time
Out-of-range inputs trigger an assertion failure

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Assigns the value from another Timestamp.
requirements: other must be a valid initialized Timestamp object

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Equivalent to copy assignment for this trivially copyable type.
requirements: other must be a valid Timestamp object

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::Now
functions.description: Creates a Timestamp for the current system time. Precision is up to nanoseconds depending on the system clock.

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::seconds
functions.description: Returns the whole seconds component since Unix epoch.

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::nanoseconds
functions.description: Returns the nanoseconds fraction within the current second (always non-negative).

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::FromTimeT
functions.description: Creates a Timestamp from a time_t interpreted as seconds since the Unix epoch. Sets nanoseconds to zero. Asserts on out-of-range values.
requirements: seconds_since_unix_epoch must map to a date in the range 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z inclusive; otherwise an assertion failure will be triggered
Assumes time_t epoch is Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z); if the platform uses a different epoch, results will be incorrect

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::FromTimePoint
functions.description: Converts a std::chrono::time_point using system_clock to a Timestamp. Asserts on out-of-range values.
requirements: time_point must correspond to a date in the range 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z inclusive; otherwise an assertion failure will be triggered
Assumes std::chrono::system_clock epoch is Unix epoch; if not, the conversion will produce incorrect results

functions.name: firebase::Timestamp::ToTimePoint
functions.signature:
template <typename Clock = std::chrono::system_clock, typename Duration = std::chrono::microseconds>
std::chrono::time_point<Clock, Duration> firebase::Timestamp::ToTimePoint() const;
functions.description: Converts this Timestamp to a std::chrono::time_point with the specified Clock and Duration (defaults to system_clock and microseconds). On overflow it saturates to Duration::min() or Duration::max().
requirements: Caller may specify Clock and Duration template parameters; the resulting time_point uses those types
Be aware that very large/small Timestamps are saturated to the representable range of Duration

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::GeoPoint
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates a GeoPoint with latitude and longitude initialized to 0.0. Useful when a sentinel or origin point is acceptable, or before assigning real coordinates.
requirements: No arguments required.
Constructs a valid, initialized GeoPoint with latitude_=0.0 and longitude_=0.0.

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::GeoPoint
functions.description: Value constructor. Creates a GeoPoint from the provided latitude and longitude values. Intended for specifying a real-world coordinate.
requirements: latitude must be within [-90, 90] degrees inclusive.
longitude must be within [-180, 180] degrees inclusive.

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::GeoPoint
functions.description: Copy constructor. Produces a new GeoPoint as a copy of another. GeoPoint is trivially copyable; copying does not throw and is equivalent to bitwise copy of its coordinates.
requirements: other must be a valid, initialized GeoPoint.

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Assigns the coordinates from another GeoPoint. For this type, assignment is trivial and equivalent to copying two doubles.
requirements: Self-assignment is allowed.
other must be a valid GeoPoint.

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Assigns from another GeoPoint by moving. For this type, moving is equivalent to copying.
requirements: Self-assignment is allowed.
other must be a valid GeoPoint; after the move it remains valid.

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::latitude

requirements: The GeoPoint object must be initialized (any constructor).

functions.name: firebase::firestore::GeoPoint::longitude
functions.description: Accessor that returns the longitude component of this GeoPoint in degrees.

requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid GeoPoint objects.

functions.name: operator!=
functions.signature: bool firebase::firestore::operator!=(const firebase::firestore::GeoPoint& lhs, const firebase::firestore::GeoPoint& rhs)
functions.description: Inequality operator for GeoPoint, defined in terms of ordering: returns true if lhs < rhs or lhs > rhs.
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid GeoPoint objects.
Note that comparison-based inequality may differ from exact floating-point bitwise inequality; behavior follows the defined ordering.

requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid GeoPoint objects.
Do not assume any tolerance or epsilon semantics unless documented elsewhere; equality relies on the ordering relation.
